judged_text: Salesforce connection setup now performs an eager token refresh (network POST to login.salesforce.com with client_secret) plus a prisma.credential.update on every service instantiation, with no expiry check and not gated on APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED, where previously construction did no network I/O and jsforce refreshed on demand. adjudication.rationale: The diff shows SalesforceCalendarService now performs an unconditional refresh-token POST to https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token and immediately updates prisma.credential (credential.update) before returning a new jsforce.Connection. There is no expiry/validity check around this refresh, and unlike other integrations in this PR it is not routed through refreshOAuthTokens nor gated by APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED. This creates a concrete, diff-grounded performance/operational concern: every time this service path runs it will incur a network round-trip plus a DB write regardless of whether the access token is still valid, which can increase load and risk rate limiting, though it’s not a strict correctness bug by itself.
